name: Amazon Rainforest
summary: The lungs of the planet facing a dangerous tipping point from combined deforestation and climate-induced megadroughts.

hotspots.title: Primary Emergent Canopy
hotspots.description: Dense multilayered canopy driving continental-scale 'flying rivers' through evapo-transpiration.
hotspots.impactCarryOn: Canopy dieback converts dense humid rainforest into dry, fire-prone degraded savannah.
hotspots.impactProtect: Reconnected biological corridors maintain moisture recycling across the South American continent.

hotspots.title: Rio Negro & Fluvial Floodplains
hotspots.description: Vital freshwater tributary network regulating regional hydration and indigenous transit.
hotspots.impactCarryOn: Record-shattering drought episodes strand riverine villages and dry up shallow oxbow lakes.
hotspots.impactProtect: Riparian buffer protections prevent riverbed silting and protect endemic aquatic biodiversity.

hotspots.title: Southern Arc of Deforestation
hotspots.description: Agricultural expansion frontier where fragmentation invites runaway wildfires.
hotspots.impactCarryOn: Fragmented forest perimeter triggers uncontrolled seasonal firestorms and carbon sink inversion.
hotspots.impactProtect: Enforced zero-deforestation mandates, satellite monitoring, and agroforestry restore frontier zones.

stats.label: Original Canopy Retained
stats.context: Percentage of pristine primary Amazonian rainforest cover remaining intact.

stats.label: Forest Carbon Balance
stats.context: Net carbon flux (negative indicates carbon sink, positive indicates net emission source).

stats.label: Dry Season Duration
stats.context: Months with less than 100mm precipitation, exacerbating wildfire flammability.

stats.label: Vertebrate Species at Risk
stats.context: Fraction of endemic flora and fauna facing severe habitat suitability loss.

carryOn.description: Surpassing the 20-25% cumulative deforestation threshold triggers irreversible dieback of 40-60% of the Amazon basin.
keyPoints: Amazon flips permanently from net carbon sink to major greenhouse gas emitter
Disruption of South American monsoon rainfall imperiling agriculture thousands of miles away
Catastrophic loss of world's richest terrestrial biodiversity

protect.description: Zero net deforestation, demarcated indigenous reserves, and high-value non-timber bioeconomy preserve forest resilience.
keyPoints: Deforestation curtailed to near-zero with 30 million hectares reforested
Empowered indigenous territorial governance across 300+ reserves
Flying rivers fully sustained, protecting continental rainfall regimes

sources.title: Amazon Assessment Report 2021
sources.institution: Science Panel for the Amazon (SPA) / United Nations SDSN
